_note: sprint is CLI-backed (./tools/sprint) and orchestrates sub-skills in reference/. A clean-context executor cannot run the CLI, so these cases are simulation-graded per skill-eval's Gotchas: grade whether the executor picks the right tier and the right sequence of steps (plan-before-code, approval gate, high-risk pipeline), not real CLI output.

evals.prompt: A user says: "sprint start: add a --json flag to the tkt ls command so it can print tickets as JSON." This adds a new option across a CLI file and its output path (coordinated, more than a cosmetic one-liner). Walk through what the sprint skill has you do.
evals.expected_output: Classifies this as normal tier, runs `sprint start`, fills acceptance.md (criteria + test plan) and plan.md (approach), presents a brief, and waits for explicit user approval before writing any code. No orient/grill/impact-analysis unless a high-risk trigger appears.
expectations: Classifies the work as normal tier (not trivial — it adds coordinated behavior across a file/output path)
Creates acceptance.md and plan.md and presents a brief BEFORE writing implementation code
Waits for explicit user approval before coding, rather than jumping straight to implementation

evals.prompt: A user says: "Fix the typo in README.md — 'commmands' should be 'commands'." Walk through how the sprint skill handles this.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this as a trivial, single-line cosmetic change that is exempt from the sprint workflow: work directly and report verification, without creating a ticket or running sprint start.
expectations: Classifies the change as trivial (single-line / cosmetic typo fix)
Does not create a ticket or run the full sprint start planning flow
Makes the fix directly and reports verification

evals.prompt: A user says: "sprint start: change the login flow to accept OAuth tokens and store the refreshed session in a cookie." Walk through what the sprint skill has you do before coding.
evals.expected_output: Classifies this as high-risk (touches auth/sessions and security-sensitive behavior), and runs the full planning pipeline — orient (research.md), grill (resolve gray areas), impact analysis with required mitigation tests, and any human checkpoint — before implementation, gated on explicit approval.
expectations: Classifies the work as high-risk because it changes authentication/session behavior
Runs the high-risk pipeline (orient / grill / impact analysis) rather than the light normal-tier path
Requires mitigation tests for high risks and waits for approval before writing code

evals.prompt: A user says: "sprint start: move the board's inline <script> out of tools/sprint-check-app/app.html into a new tools/sprint-check-app/static/board.js." It touches every board user, so it is high-risk and you are in the orient (research) step. So far the research found that no source file imports app.html, and ran `git grep -n app.html -- tests/`, which printed one hit: `tests/board-spec.js:12: const html = fs.readFileSync(APP_HTML, 'utf8')`. Is the search for app.html's readers done? If not, say exactly what the research does next and what it records.
evals.expected_output: Says the reader search is not done: a search limited to importers and to tests/ is not enough. The research re-runs the grep repo-wide with no path or type filter, for the file name and the moved symbols, looks for readers that never import the file (tests in other languages, scripts that grep its text or fetch the page over HTTP), and lists and classifies every hit in research.md before moving on.
expectations: Says the search is not done because it was limited to importers and to tests/
Re-runs the grep over the whole repo with no path or type filter, for the file name and the moved or changed symbols
Names the kinds of non-import readers to look for: tests in other languages, and scripts that grep its text or fetch it over HTTP
Lists and classifies every hit (must change / still fine) in research.md before the research moves on

evals.prompt: You are in a project with the sprint skill. Ticket t-1111 (a screen-mockup .pen file plus exported PNGs, nothing else changed) has `demo: true` in its frontmatter. The user says: "sprint complete". Which gates run at close, what model does the evaluator get, and may you set `eval_override` to skip the evaluator to save time?
evals.expected_output: Light close: only security-review and the binding evaluator run; the advisory reviewer and the rest of wrapup are skipped; the evaluator runs on Haiku; eval_override is never set because the evaluator is never dropped.
expectations: States that the close keeps exactly security-review and the evaluator, and skips the advisory reviewer and the rest of wrapup
States the evaluator is dispatched on Haiku (and security-review runs inline on the session model)
Refuses to set eval_override: the binding evaluator is never dropped, even in a light close

evals.prompt: A user says: "sprint start: research how three competing CLIs handle plugin discovery and write it up as docs/research/plugins.md." Nothing else in the repo changes. What do you do about the close path, and who decides?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes docs/research work, proposes the light close (offers `tkt demo <id> on`) with the reason, and leaves the decision to the user rather than applying it automatically.
expectations: Recognizes the request as docs/research work and proposes the light close (demo mode), giving a reason
Offers or names setting the flag on the ticket (`tkt demo <id> on` or `demo: true`) rather than applying it silently
Treats it as the user's election: asks or waits instead of auto-applying; does not choose it as a risk tier

evals.prompt: You ran a normal-tier sprint to fix an off-by-one in `lib/paginate.sh`. At close the diff is exactly `lib/paginate.sh` and its existing test `tests/paginate.sh`, which asserts the page count for a 10-item list. No new files, no hook or build-wiring changes. What tier decision do you make, where do you record it, and which gates still run?
evals.expected_output: The diff qualifies for bugfix: a single logic file plus its covering test. Plan ran as normal; at close write `Tier: bugfix` in plan.md's Sign-off. The binding evaluator still runs; the advisory reviewer and heavy wrapup are skipped.
expectations: Concludes the diff qualifies for the bugfix tier (single logic file plus its covering test, none of the four not-trivial triggers)
Says to record `Tier: bugfix` in plan.md's `## Sign-off`, as a close-time downgrade, not chosen at start
Says the binding evaluator still runs and only the advisory reviewer and heavy wrapup are skipped

evals.prompt: You ran a normal-tier sprint for a small fix. At close the diff is `lib/paginate.sh`, its test `tests/paginate.sh`, and a NEW file `tests/fixtures/pages.txt` the test reads. Can you downgrade to the bugfix tier? Say which gates run.
evals.expected_output: No: a new file beyond the test is one of the four not-trivial triggers, so the sprint stays normal with the reviewer and full wrapup.
expectations: Concludes the sprint stays normal tier and does not write `Tier: bugfix`
Names the new file (beyond the covering test) as the trigger that blocks the downgrade
Says the full gate set still runs (reviewer, wrapup and the binding evaluator)

evals.prompt: You are Claude Code in a consumer project (not canon's repo). The sprint skill tells you to `Read skills/sprint/reference/start-checklist.md`, but there is no `skills/` directory at the project root. In the same project, Codex is also used. Where do you read it from in each harness, and what do you do if the file is not found there?
evals.expected_output: Claude Code: `.claude/skills/sprint/reference/start-checklist.md`; Codex/Pi: `.agents/skills/sprint/reference/start-checklist.md`; canon's install symlinks into its real skills tree.
expectations: Resolves the path to `.claude/skills/...` for Claude Code
Resolves the path to `.agents/skills/...` for Codex/Pi
Treats the `skills/` path as relative to canon's own repo, not a missing file to report as an error
